clue.text: Theatrical phantom is pelting front of gallery crowd (12, two words)

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: to pepper is to pelt with shot or missiles
the opening letter of gallery
a host is a great crowd or multitude

explanation.surface: A stage ghost is being pelted by the crowd in the gallery, the cheap seats of a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: PEPPER'S GHOST is a Victorian stage illusion in which a figure reflected in angled glass appears as a transparent ghost on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The illusion, named after the scientist John Henry Pepper, was a celebrated theatrical spectre effect.

clue.text: Young salmon, light brown, feature of Mull seafood restaurant?

blocks.note: par (parr) is a young salmon
a light brown colour

explanation.surface: A menu on the Scottish isle of Mull offers young salmon, lightly browned.
explanation.walkthrough: Mull is a Hebridean island, so the dish is Scottish; partan is the Scots word for an edible crab.
explanation.definitionFit: A partan is a crab in Scots, just what a seafood restaurant on a Scottish island would serve.

clue.text: Bomber attack sounded clearly under power

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts one piece below the other

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for power
rang means sounded like a bell

explanation.surface: A bombing raid resounded loudly under the force of the engines.
explanation.walkthrough: Prang is RAF slang for a bombing raid, as well as for a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: In wartime RAF slang a prang was a bombing attack on a target.

clue.text: One bit of carpeting taken up in flat for hermit

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking something up lifts it so it reads from the bottom
the lifted letters are placed inside the next word

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
a rug is a small piece of carpet
a pad is a flat, a place to live

explanation.surface: A rug in a flat is lifted, perhaps for a recluse who lives there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hermit' looks like a recluse but is short for hermit crab, whose family is the Paguridae.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagurid is a crab of the hermit-crab family, so a hermit in the crustacean sense.

clue.text: Get going again, including start of dating bird

indicators.note: a word including another has it inside
the start of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: to restart is to get going once more
the opening letter of dating

explanation.surface: Someone gets back into dating again, bird-watching included.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a small songbird of the thrush family with a reddish tail.

clue.text: It's no longer tasteful, when cast 'bust a leg'

definitions.note: no longer marks an obsolete word

indicators.note: to cast is to throw, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An actor is told to 'bust a leg', a clumsy version of break a leg, and it is no longer in good taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' hints at a theatre company after the good-luck phrase, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustable is an obsolete word for tasty or pleasant to the palate.

clue.text: Eager hoe-down circling street

indicators.note: circling something goes all round it

blocks.note: the hay (hey) is a country dance
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Keen dancers whirl round the street at a country hoe-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasty means hurried and impatient, quick to act, as an eager person is.

clue.text: Fish from Spain circling river

indicators.note: circling something goes all round it

blocks.note: of can mean from, as in 'of noble birth'
R is the abbreviation for river
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A fish from Spain swims round a river.
explanation.walkthrough: OF wraps round R, with E for Spain added.
explanation.definitionFit: The orfe is a freshwater fish, the golden form of the ide.

clue.text: Sandwich that's appetising, with egg in

indicators.note: the letter is placed in the middle of the word

blocks.note: appetising food is tasty
an egg is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: An appetising sandwich has an egg filling.
explanation.walkthrough: A toasty is an informal British name for a toasted sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: A toasty is a toasted sandwich, often filled and sealed in a sandwich maker.

clue.text: Accepted bishop's mild exclamation: 'Bedad!'

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for accepted
RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title
a gentle interjection of surprise or pleasure

explanation.surface: A bishop, on being accepted, lets out a gentle Irish oath.
explanation.walkthrough: ARRAH is an Irish interjection of surprise; 'Bedad!' (by God) is another Irish exclamation, so it serves as the example-style definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are Irish interjections expressing surprise or emotion, so one stands in for the other.

clue.text: Cause of red eyes poor hen had treated

indicators.note: treated things are processed and altered, so the letters change order

blocks.note: ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A poorly hen with sore red eyes is given treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'treated' does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodophane is a red pigment found in the retinal cones of some birds and fish, giving their eyes a reddish hue.

clue.text: Book size said in Scotland to contain pictures

indicators.note: one word is made to contain another, holding it within its letters

blocks.note: quo is the Scots form of quoth, meaning said
pictures collectively are art

explanation.surface: A book's format is described in Scots terms as one holding illustrations.
explanation.walkthrough: QU-ART-O: the pictures sit inside the Scots word for said.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarto is a page format made by folding a printed sheet twice, giving four leaves; it names a standard book size.

clue.text: Crushing formerly hurt struggling clubs in grip of problem

indicators.note: struggling suggests writhing about, so the letters are thrown out of order
being in the grip of something means being held inside it

blocks.note: letters to rearrange
C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards
a thing can be a problem, as in having a thing about something

explanation.surface: Hurt and struggling, a golfer crushes his clubs while wrestling with a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: THRUTCH is a dialect word meaning to press or squeeze; 'formerly' marks the sense as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrutch is to thrust, press or squeeze hard, so thrutching is crushing in an old usage.

clue.text: What skin cream soothes, treating a red gash

indicators.note: treating something works it over and alters it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A skin cream soothes by treating a red gash.
explanation.walkthrough: RHAGADES are cracks or fissures in the skin, especially at the corners of the mouth, so the whole clue also reads as a description of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhagades are painful skin fissures, exactly the kind of sore a soothing ointment is applied to.

clue.text: Speedster to drive round, holding on

indicators.note: turning round sends the word back the other way
a word holding another keeps it inside itself

blocks.note: to put is to drive or propel, as in putting the shot
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fast driver is told to drive around while holding on tight.
explanation.walkthrough: A ton-up boy was a 1950s-60s British motorcyclist who rode at a hundred miles an hour (a ton).
explanation.definitionFit: Ton-up describes someone who rides at a hundred mph or more, so a reckless fast motorcyclist.

clue.text: Models that shouldn't be missed

blocks.note: first meaning: people who pose for an artist or photographer
second meaning: easy chances in sport, such as a catch no fielder should drop

explanation.surface: Fashion models so striking that nobody should miss seeing them.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists' models sit for portraits; in sport an easy chance is called a sitter because it sits there waiting to be taken.

clue.text: Prop not yet solid admits bloody lifting inside

indicators.note: something that admits another lets it inside
in a down clue, lifting raises a word so it reads upwards
confirms the lifted word ends up within the outer one

blocks.note: unset means not yet hardened
the colour of blood

explanation.surface: A support not yet set hard lets a bloody thing lift inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An underset is a support or prop placed beneath something; as a verb it means to prop up.

clue.text: The feminine Parisian kid mostly appears in this uniform

indicators.note: mostly means all but a little, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: la is the feminine form of 'the' in French
a youth is a young person, a kid

explanation.surface: A young girl from Paris turns up dressed in a particular uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers gives layout the sense of an outfit or set of gear, which lets it stand for uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A layout can mean a full outfit or kit laid out for use, and a uniform is such an outfit.

clue.text: Flowers showing trouble rising in leaf divisions

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word reads from bottom to top
the risen word is placed inside the next

blocks.note: lobes are the rounded divisions of a leaf
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Flowers show trouble growing up through their leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelias are garden bedding plants with small blue or purple flowers.

clue.text: Names from the past I'm among shortly making comeback

indicators.note: to be among something is to be placed in its midst
a comeback returns the way it came, so the letters run back to front

blocks.note: anon means soon, shortly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone says they are among old names that are soon to return.
explanation.walkthrough: AN(I'M)ON is built first, then the whole is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomina is the Latin plural of nomen, the clan name of a Roman citizen, so names from antiquity.

clue.text: Maybe ironic address to friend year after sack?

blocks.note: a mat can be a sack made of matting, used for coffee and the like
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A sacked worker, a year on, greets a pal with a sarcastic friendly word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the year at the end. MATY (matey) is the chummy word often used with mock friendliness, as in 'Listen, matey'.
explanation.definitionFit: Matey is a familiar form of address between mates, frequently used with a sarcastic edge.

clue.text: Rounded lump mother found on fruit

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece found on another sits above it

blocks.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
a large juicy fruit

explanation.surface: Mother discovers a round lump on a piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A mamelon is a small rounded hillock or protuberance, from the French for nipple.

clue.text: Murphy giving a hand alongside son

indicators.note: alongside sets two pieces next to each other in a row

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
pud is a childish word for a hand or paw

explanation.surface: A man called Murphy lends a hand next to his son.
explanation.walkthrough: Murphy is slang for a potato, from its Irish associations.
explanation.definitionFit: Spud and murphy are both informal words for a potato, so they are slang synonyms.

clue.text: Find out about Switzerland for feature of downhill skiing

indicators.note: about means placed around another word

blocks.note: to suss out is to find out
CH is the international code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: Someone researches Switzerland for a feature on downhill skiing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature' suggests a magazine article, but here it means a characteristic part.
explanation.definitionFit: A schuss is a straight, fast run downhill on skis, a typical element of the sport.

clue.text: Application for military uniform left in money kept in accounts

indicators.note: one letter is placed inside the word that follows

blocks.note: banco is bank money, a money of account rather than coin
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Pay for a soldier's uniform is left in the books as a sum of account.
explanation.walkthrough: Blanco is a whitening or colouring compound soldiers applied to webbing belts and straps.
explanation.definitionFit: Blanco is a cleaning compound applied to military webbing, so it is something put onto uniform.

clue.text: Bug, obscure, appearing on opening of speedwell (literally)

indicators.note: in a down clue, appearing on another piece means sitting above it
the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: obs is the dictionary abbreviation for obscure
the first letter is taken, and 'literally' asks for its spelt-out name

explanation.surface: An obscure insect turns up on a speedwell flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'literally' asks for the letter's name as a word, ESS, rather than the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to pester or preoccupy them, and to obsess them is to preoccupy them constantly.

clue.text: Cut going into what's mixed etc, old-style pie thereof?

indicators.note: something going into another ends up inside it
mixed letters are jumbled out of their order

blocks.note: the letters of etc in a new order
to hew is to cut

explanation.surface: A cut of meat goes into a mixture of this and that, making an old-fashioned pie of the stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: A chewet was an old pie of chopped meat and other things mixed together, which is the joke of 'thereof?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewet is an obsolete word for a small pie or pasty of minced meat and seasonings.

clue.text: Our lot will trap deer in decline (old)

indicators.note: trapping something holds it shut inside

blocks.note: our lot means us, we
the elk is a large deer

explanation.surface: We will catch a deer whose numbers are falling.
explanation.definitionFit: Welke is an old spelling of welk, to wither or fade, so to decline.

clue.text: Measure of species changes lecturer showed in film

indicators.note: something shown in another appears within it

blocks.note: cine is short for cinematograph film
L is the abbreviation for lecturer

explanation.surface: A biology lecturer shows a film about how species change.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a cline is a gradient of variation in a species across its geographical range.

clue.text: Dim northerner needing to grasp difference ultimately between right and left

indicators.note: ultimately points to the end, so only the closing letter counts
placed between two things it is flanked by them on either side

blocks.note: to have is to hold or grasp
R is the abbreviation for right
the final letter of difference
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A slow-witted northerner needs help telling right from left.
explanation.walkthrough: Haverel is Scots for a foolish chatterer, so 'northerner' marks it as a Scottish word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots a haverel is a half-wit or one who talks nonsense, so a dim person from the north.

clue.text: A rag banned from local benefice as depravity

indicators.note: what is banned from a place is shut out of it

blocks.note: taken as written
a vicarage is the house or living of a parish vicar

explanation.surface: A scandal sheet is banned from the parish house as depraved.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag is a newspaper of low quality, but the two words are only letters removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Vice means wickedness or immoral conduct, which is what depravity is.

clue.text: Cats forming line in Irish festival

indicators.note: the letter is set inside the word that follows

blocks.note: a feis is an Irish festival of music and dance
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Cats line up at an Irish festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Felis is the zoological genus of the smaller cats, including the domestic cat.

clue.text: Love making flip in second fruit tonic?

indicators.note: a flip turns a word over so it runs the other way
the flipped word is put inside the following pieces

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a citrus fruit
love is zero in tennis, nil

explanation.surface: A lover takes a quick fruity tonic drink in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: Slimline tonic is a low-calorie version of the mixer, so the question mark flags that the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Slimline is the label on a low-calorie tonic water, so a tonic may be described that way.

clue.text: Pear yielding dry unit (not vin)

indicators.note: not marks the letters that follow it as removed from the word

blocks.note: sec is dry, of wine
the kelvin is the SI unit of temperature
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pear gives a dry measure, but no wine, as the French would say.
explanation.walkthrough: The French touches 'sec' and 'vin' suggest wine-tasting, but vin is just the letters removed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seckel is a small sweet American variety of pear.

clue.text: Secret societies? They can make your hair curl

definitions.text: They can make your hair curl

blocks.note: first meaning: Chinese secret associations, the plural of tong

blocks.clueFragment: They can make your hair curl
blocks.note: second meaning: heated curling irons

explanation.surface: Secret societies are frightening enough to make your hair curl.
explanation.definitionFit: A tong is a Chinese secret society, and curling tongs are a hairdressing tool.

clue.text: Senses we stirred with this result of adding a modicum of sugar?

definitions.text: result of adding a modicum of sugar?

indicators.note: stirred things are swirled round and mixed up

blocks.note: letters to rearrange
more letters for the mix

explanation.surface: Our senses detect, once stirred, the slight sweetness of a little sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: The stirring fits the picture of sugar going into a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A modicum of sugar makes something only slightly sweet, and that quality is the abstract noun asked for.
